prompt: Validate a 24-hour clock string. Complete the isValidTime method so it returns true only for times "00:00" through "23:59" written with exactly two digits on each side of the colon, using String.matches.
explanation: String.matches tests whether the WHOLE string fits the pattern, so no ^ or $ anchors are needed. The hour cannot be a simple [0-2][0-9] because that would accept 24 through 29; instead an alternation ([01][0-9]|2[0-3]) allows 00-19 or 20-23. Minutes are easier since every value 00-59 fits [0-5][0-9], and the literal colon separates the two parts.
hints: s.matches(regex) already requires the regex to cover the entire string.
Split the hour into two cases: first digit 0 or 1 allows any second digit, but first digit 2 only allows 0-3. Group the alternation in parentheses.
Minutes are one range: [0-5][0-9]. Put a plain : between the hour group and the minutes.
